title: Add Private deployment operator + auditor role templates (env/cluster scoped)
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Adds built-in role templates for Private deployment operators and auditors with explicit environment/cluster scopes.
Includes example role bindings for IdP group mapping patterns commonly used in Private installs.
Introduces guardrails to prevent org-wide grants for cluster-admin permissions by default (lint rule + template structure).
body: Summary: This PR adds a set of built-in RBAC v2 role templates intended for Redwood Private deployments, focused on common operator and auditor workflows. The templates are explicitly scoped (environment and cluster) and are designed to support least-privilege, separation of duties, and evidence-friendly auditability. Context/motivation: Private customers (and internal pilots) have asked for clear “day-2 operations” roles (upgrade, health checks, log viewing) and separate read-only/audit roles that can export audit logs without granting mutation privileges. We also saw multiple support cases where Dedicated/Private admins were blocked due to missing template permissions or where customers over-granted Org Admin to solve an operator need (SUP-48288, SUP-48219). This PR is part of ENG-18444 (role template generator + templates) and aligns with the scope model decisions being rolled into PM-661. What’s included (new templates): 1) Private Deployment Operator (cluster-scoped): intended for on-call/SRE-style operators to manage day-2 cluster operations without org-wide admin rights. Grants include read access to cluster state, view deployments, view runtime health, initiate safe restarts/rollouts where supported, and access operational logs/diagnostics. Explicitly excludes identity/role management, billing, org settings, and key/secret material beyond what is required for operational workflows. 2) Private Deployment Admin (environment-scoped with cluster sub-scope examples): intended for platform administrators responsible for Private environments. Grants include cluster lifecycle actions (create/upgrade/scale), configure deployment-level settings, manage routing policy artifacts tied to the environment, and manage environment-scoped retention/export configuration where applicable. Excludes org-wide identity management by default; customers can compose with Org/User Admin templates if they want a single “super-admin” role. 3) Private Read-only Auditor (environment-scoped): read-only across configuration and operational state + ability to access audit logs UI/API read endpoints. No export by default (export is a separate permission in RBAC v2 due to data exfil risk). 4) Private Audit Exporter (environment-scoped): minimal role focused on exporting audit logs (and associated export job status) without access to broader configuration changes. Intended for compliance teams / GRC / SIEM pipeline operators. 5) Private Security Auditor (environment-scoped): read access to security-relevant configuration (SSO/IdP mappings if exposed in Private control plane, KMS/HSM integration status, break-glass event summaries if surfaced), plus audit log read. Export is optional via composition with Private Audit Exporter. Scope model + examples: Templates are written to be used with RBAC v2 scopes: org -> environment -> cluster. This PR includes concrete examples showing: - A cluster-scoped binding for operators (e.g., “ops-oncall” group gets Private Deployment Operator on cluster prod-us-east-1a). - An environment-scoped binding for auditors (e.g., “grc-audit” group gets Private Read-only Auditor on environment prod). - A separate binding for SIEM export automation (e.g., “siem-exporter” service principal gets Private Audit Exporter on environment prod). Design notes / guardrails: - Separation of duties: export is separated from read by default. Review feedback requested this after seeing customers inadvertently grant export to broad read-only roles. - Avoid org-wide cluster-admin defaults: the templates are structured so that cluster mutation permissions are only present in the operator/admin templates and the documentation examples bind them to cluster or environment scopes. - Composition-friendly: customers can compose templates by assigning multiple roles to the same principal at different scopes; we intentionally avoided “one role to rule them all.” Files/areas changed (high level): - templates/private/*.yaml: new role templates for private operators/auditors/admins. - examples/private/*.yaml: example RoleBinding manifests for common IdP group mapping patterns. - docs/role-templates/private.md: brief rationale + how-to for choosing templates and scoping them. - lint/policy-lint-rules.yaml: added a rule to flag org-scope bindings for cluster-admin permissions in template examples (warn-level for now). Permissions referenced: This PR only references existing permission strings from the canonical registry (no new permissions introduced here). Notably included: audit.logs.read, audit.logs.export, private.cluster.read, private.cluster.upgrade, private.cluster.scale, private.cluster.diagnostics.read, private.runtime.logs.read, private.routing.policy.read/update (env-scoped), private.deployment.settings.read/update (env-scoped). If any of these strings change during migration, templates will be updated in lockstep (ENG-18444 tracks generator+versioning). Testing: - policy-bundle lint (naming, duplicates, forbidden org-scope examples) - template compile + snapshot test (ensures generated bundle includes new templates) - YAML schema validation for RoleTemplate and RoleBinding examples Rollout/consumers: - Redwood Private installer will start referencing these templates for bootstrap defaults in a follow-up (tracked in ENG-18410). - Console role template picker will surface these under “Private deployments” category once the console wiring lands (separate PR). Risks: - Over/under-scoping: if customers bind operator roles at environment scope, they will grant multi-cluster mutation. This PR mitigates via examples + lint warnings, but enforcement ultimately happens in the control plane’s scope evaluation. - Permission drift: if permissions are renamed/deprecated, templates must be regenerated. Follow-ups: - Add a “Private Break-glass Operator” template once break-glass flow is fully specified end-to-end (Security + SecOps). - Consider a dedicated “Private Read-only Support” role for Redwood support engineers (internal use, guarded). Review notes: Marcus requested we split audit export out of the auditor template and ensure no identity/role mutation permissions appear in the operator role. Vivek requested we include upgrade/scale actions in Private Deployment Admin and keep operator cluster-scoped by default. Colin validated the examples match how pilot customers map IdP groups and asked for a service principal example for SIEM export. All changes addressed in the final commit. Changelog: New templates are additive and do not change any existing role definitions. Existing bundles remain valid. CI: All checks green (lint, schema validate, snapshot, unit tests).
commits: Add Private Deployment Operator + Admin role templates
Add Private Read-only Auditor + Audit Exporter templates
Add env/cluster scoped role binding examples for common IdP group mappings
Add lint rule to warn on org-scope bindings for cluster-admin permissions
Docs: private role templates selection + composition guidance
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security Eng): The auditor template currently includes audit.logs.export. We should split export into a separate role (data exfil risk) and keep auditor read-only by default. Also please confirm operator role does not include any org/user/role permissions.

Jordan Lee (Author): Agreed. I split export into a new Private Audit Exporter template and updated the auditor to read-only. Operator template is restricted to private.* operational permissions; no org/user/role/billing permissions included. Added examples showing composition when export is needed.

Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments PM): For Private Deployment Admin, can we include cluster upgrade + scale actions at environment scope? Operators should stay cluster-scoped. Also add an example for multi-cluster prod env where admin is env-scoped but operators are per-cluster.

Jordan Lee (Author): Updated admin template to include upgrade/scale and added the requested example. Operator remains cluster-scoped in examples; added a lint warning when binding operator/admin templates at org scope.

Colin O'Donnell (Solutions Eng): The SIEM export automation for pilots uses a service principal, not a human group. Can we add a rolebinding example with a non-human principal name and a note about least privilege / rotating credentials?
Jordan Lee (Author): Added examples/private/rolebindings-prod-env.yaml with a service principal binding and notes on scoping + credential rotation. Thanks.

Ines Carvalho (Tenancy/scoping): Small nit: examples should use environment IDs not display names to avoid confusion. Also the cluster scope format should match what the control plane emits (env:<id>/cluster:<id>).
Jordan Lee (Author): Updated examples to use env_id/cluster_id forms and aligned scope strings with the latest control plane spec.
